solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Buyer gets a third off drink

indicators.note: losing a third means one of the word's three syllables, here the opening one, is cut away

explanation.surface: A shopper is offered money off a bottle of something alcoholic.
explanation.walkthrough: PURCHASER has nine letters, so a third off removes PUR, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a drink taken straight after another, such as beer after a shot of spirits.

clue.text: Vehicle with excellent emperor carrying British cop abroad

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A fine car and an emperor transport a British policeman somewhere overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' applies only to the excellent piece, which holds the British letter; the vehicle and emperor stand either side.
explanation.definitionFit: A carabinero is a member of the Spanish or Italian police or frontier guard, hence a foreign policeman.

clue.text: Title of respect accepted by sailor, say, in foreign language

indicators.note: what is accepted by something is taken inside it

parts.note: U is a Burmese title of respect, as in U Thant
e.g. means for example, i.e. say

explanation.surface: A sailor picks up a polite form of address in some foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the Burmese honorific familiar from the UN Secretary-General U Thant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuareg is the Berber language of the Tuareg people of the Sahara, so a foreign language.

clue.text: Instrument of torture making long marks externally

indicators.note: marks placed externally sit on the outside, wrapping around the other piece

parts.note: scars are marks on the skin
to pine is to long for

explanation.surface: A torture device that leaves lasting marks on its victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the marks but is a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarpines were an iron boot-like device used to crush the feet in torture, per Chambers.

clue.text: With temperature dropping, old printer gets wig

indicators.note: a letter that drops out falls away and is no longer part of the word

parts.note: William Caxton, the first English printer
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A historic printer, losing his warmth, puts on a hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T from CAXTON.
explanation.definitionFit: A caxon is an old kind of wig, an obsolete term listed in Chambers.

clue.text: Disturbing behaviour from hag growling

indicators.note: taken from means the letters are lifted out of the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A snarling old crone is behaving in an unsettling way.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive, troublesome behaviour or deliberate trouble-making.

clue.text: Game very good — gosh, it makes money!

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means very good or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a game that earns money.
explanation.walkthrough: PI for 'very good' is a crossword favourite from 'pious'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupiah is the currency of Indonesia, so it is a form of money.

clue.text: Chum that's certain to be tied up in study

indicators.note: being tied up in something means held within it
in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top, so backwards

explanation.surface: A friend who is sure to be busy with schoolwork.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' turns the word for certain backwards before it is tied inside the chum.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination, which is a kind of study.

clue.text: A king entering square in small opening

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: of or in the nostrils

indicators.note: what enters something goes inside it

parts.note: nine is a square number, three squared
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch steps into a square inside some little gap.
explanation.walkthrough: N(A R)INE. 'Square' looks like a town square but is a number that is a perfect square.
explanation.definitionFit: Narine means relating to the nostrils, which are small openings in the nose.

clue.text: Water tub knocked over in parliamentary house

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, so in a down clue it reads the other way

parts.note: a dan is a small tub, a dialect word in Chambers

explanation.surface: A tub of water is upset inside the parliament building.
explanation.definitionFit: Seanad Éireann is the Irish senate, the upper house of the Oireachtas, Ireland's parliament.

clue.text: Adult in basic dwelling no longer arrogant

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a hut is a simple dwelling
A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up living in a shack has lost any haughtiness.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside HUT. 'No longer' belongs to the definition: the word is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Haut is an archaic form of haughty, so it meant proud or arrogant in older English.

clue.text: Physical problem you finally found in nasty cage with pain as before

indicators.note: as before flags an old-fashioned spelling of the word for pain
nasty suggests something messed up, so the letters are jumbled
finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: ake is an old spelling of ache

explanation.surface: An old ailment that turns up in a horrible cage along with an ache.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry is hyphenated, AGUE-CAKE; 'found in' places the last letter of 'you' among the jumbled cage letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague-cake was a swelling of the spleen or liver thought to result from ague, a bodily disorder.

clue.text: A device that'd stop you backing horse

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A gadget to stop you betting on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing horse' reads as placing a bet, but backing reverses the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse noted for speed and stamina, originating in Arabia.

clue.text: Tincture applied by artist — odd for Raeburn?

parts.note: or is the heraldic tincture gold

explanation.surface: A colour applied by a painter; was it unusual for Raeburn?
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Raeburn was a Scottish portrait painter, so 'for Raeburn' asks for the Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Orra is Scots for odd, in the sense of occasional or spare, the dialect a Scot such as Raeburn would use.

clue.text: See a troll wandering round edge of forest with beaky projection

indicators.note: going round something encloses it
letters that wander roam away from their places into a new order
an edge is an end letter, here the rear end of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A troll roams through the woods, beak-like nose protruding.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SEE A TROLL gives ROSELLATE, which goes round the T.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostellate means having a rostellum, a small beak-like process found on some plants and animals.

clue.text: Our stairs tricky? It's the knee muscle

indicators.note: something tricky is awkward and twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Awkward stairs at home are blamed for a damaged knee.
explanation.definitionFit: The sartorius is the long thigh muscle that flexes the knee, attaching just below it.

clue.text: Wild beast in stories about love

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A savage animal appears in tales of romance.
explanation.walkthrough: AN(O)A.
explanation.definitionFit: The anoa is a small wild buffalo of Sulawesi, a wild animal.

clue.text: Musical instrument without note for tuning

parts.note: orchestras tune to the note A

explanation.surface: An instrument that cannot be tuned because it lacks the note.
explanation.definitionFit: The sansa is an African thumb piano, also called the mbira or kalimba.

clue.text: Marine mammal left in high water floundering

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters thrash into a new order

explanation.surface: A sea creature stranded at high tide, struggling to move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floundering' tempts as a fish (a flounder), fitting the sea picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The right whale is a large baleen whale, so named as the 'right' one for whalers to hunt.

clue.text: Left-winger on the up — this person's distorted, old-fashioned

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: this person is the setter, I; I've is I has, read as possessive

explanation.surface: A rising socialist admits being bent, and dated too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person's' is read as 'I have', I'VE. 'Old-fashioned' belongs to the definition: the word is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortive is an archaic word for twisted, from the same root as torture and contort.

clue.text: Animals together no longer, everything going topsy-turvy

indicators.note: topsy-turvy means upside down, so in a down clue the letters run the other way

parts.note: sam is an obsolete word for together

explanation.surface: Creatures that no longer stay together, everything turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the obsolete SAM. Both pieces together are reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelids kept as pack animals, an example of animals.

clue.text: Language of "Abide With Me" author brings converts

parts.note: Henry Francis Lyte wrote the hymn; 'of' makes it possessive

explanation.surface: The words of a well-known hymn writer win people over.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as PROSE + LYTE'S: the 'of' becomes the possessive ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Proselytes are people converted from one religion or opinion to another.

clue.text: Bad carpenter lacking art producing puncture once

indicators.note: bad implies poorly put together, so the letters are reordered
lacking something means it is missing, so those letters are taken out

explanation.surface: A clumsy woodworker without skill makes a hole in something.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ART out of CARPENTER, leaving CPENER, then rearrange. 'Once' marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Percen is an obsolete form of pierce, meaning to make a hole through.

clue.text: Winter vehicle about to get covered in slimy stuff

indicators.note: something covered in another is wrapped inside it

explanation.surface: A car in winter about to be coated in grime.
explanation.walkthrough: SNO(CA)T.
explanation.definitionFit: A snocat is a tracked vehicle built for travel over snow, used in polar regions.

clue.text: Like star losing head, becoming sucker

indicators.note: losing its head means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: stellar means like or of a star

explanation.surface: A former star, decapitated, becomes a gullible victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' reads as a dupe, but it is the botanical shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellar is a variant of tiller, a shoot or sucker that springs from the base of a plant.

clue.text: Monster runs off into hovel generating smoke

indicators.note: going into something puts it inside

parts.note: a sty is a filthy dwelling

indicators.note: off means removed, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A monster flees into a shack, which then starts smoking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' at the end reads as a verb for the hovel, but it is a noun naming a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stogey is a long cheap cigar, and a cigar is a smoke.

clue.text: Scottish storyteller and humorist entertaining English

indicators.note: a host entertaining a guest holds them within

parts.note: Edward Lear, writer of nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A Scottish teller of tales and a comic writer amuse an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: LE(E)AR. 'Storyteller' here is a euphemism for someone who tells lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Leear is a Scots spelling of liar, and a liar is a teller of stories in the sense of falsehoods.

clue.text: Disciple looking back around American temple

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the letters read in reverse
something around another encloses it

parts.note: a son, as in 'son of the prophets', is a disciple

explanation.surface: A follower glances back at an American place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: SO(A)N is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A naos is the inner chamber of a Greek temple, and by extension the temple itself.

clue.text: A female educated to make porcelain

parts.note: the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A woman is trained to create fine china.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is Willy Russell's play about a woman studying with the Open University.
explanation.definitionFit: Arita is a Japanese porcelain from the town of Arita in Kyushu.

clue.text: Musical performance lacking extremes — evensong enough for me?

indicators.note: without its extremes the word loses both of its end letters

parts.note: a concert is a musical performance

explanation.surface: A churchgoer finds one evening service plenty, without extra music.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the voice of the person themself: one service, evensong, is enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A oncer is someone who goes to church only once on a Sunday, so a single service suffices.

clue.text: See one stroll around rendering a form of verse

indicators.note: around suggests letters moved about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lone walker wanders about composing poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a prompt to look; the nine letters of 'one stroll' are the whole fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A stornello is a short Italian folk song or verse form, often of three lines.

clue.text: Slouch about, having lost heart in muggy Scottish weather

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: to mooch is to wander aimlessly

explanation.surface: Someone droops dispiritedly about in damp, close Scottish weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Moch is a Scots word for warm, misty, humid weather.

clue.text: Robbery has bishop confronting convict

indicators.note: confronting means standing face to face, so one piece is set before the other

parts.note: an old lag is a convict

explanation.surface: A clergyman faces a criminal over a theft.
explanation.definitionFit: Blag is British slang for a robbery, especially a violent one.

clue.text: Heaped volume — a medicated paste to be spread about

indicators.note: a paste spread about something covers it, holding it inside

parts.note: a cerate is a stiff ointment of wax and oil

explanation.surface: A large quantity of medicinal ointment is to be smeared around.
explanation.walkthrough: A + CER(V)ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Acervate is a botanical term meaning growing in heaps or clusters.

clue.text: Asian meat dish Greek characters sent back

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way it came, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Greek diners return an Asian meat dish to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people sending food back, but these are letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sate is a variant spelling of satay, skewered grilled meat from South-East Asia.

clue.text: Boy faces difficulty with adult line of poem

parts.note: a net is a trap, a fix to be caught in
A is the abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A lad struggles over a line in a poem with grown-up help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line of poem' looks like the definition, but the line is the railway and the definition is 'of poem'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonnetary is a rare adjective meaning relating to or of the nature of a sonnet, a kind of poem.
